MULTIFAN-CL to opal: south-west Pacific albacore

Bridging the 2024 WCPFC south Pacific albacore diagnostic model, a two-region MULTIFAN-CL model, to a single-region opal model

Author

Nicholas Ducharme-Barth

Published

November 3, 2026

Setup: read the caches 
# Code is shown (folded) in the HTML version and hidden in the PDF.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = knitr::is_html_output())
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

bridge = readRDS(file.path("data", "swpo-alb-mfcl-bridge.rds"))
oc     = readRDS(file.path("data", "swpo-alb-opal-cache.rds"))
lfd    = readRDS(file.path("data", "swpo-alb-lf-diagnostics.rds"))

theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
          theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))
fmt = function(x, d = 2) ifelse(is.na(x), "", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ","))
sci = function(x, d = 1) formatC(x, format = "e", digits = d)
pct = function(x, d = 1) paste0(fmt(100 * x, d), "%")

L  = bridge$likelihood
TS = bridge$timeseries
TR = oc$trajectory
RP = oc$replays
PR = oc$profile
P  = lfd$profiles
lb_mfcl = oc$log_B0_mfcl
step_col = c(M0 = "grey20", M1 = "#7D3C98", M2 = "#2471A3", M3 = "#C0392B")
model_col = c("MFCL M3" = "grey20", O0 = "#7D3C98", O1 = "#2471A3", `O1-mid` = "#C0392B")
sb_at = function(s, y) TS[step == s & year == y, sb]
dep_at = function(s, y) TS[step == s & year == y, depletion]
o1_lb = oc$o1$par[["log_B0"]]
o1m_lb = oc$o1_mid$par[["log_B0"]]

1 Overview

This document converts the 2024 stock assessment of south Pacific albacore (Thunnus alalunga) (Teears et al. 2024), a two-region MULTIFAN-CL (MFCL, Fournier et al. 1998; Davies et al. 2025) model, into opal, an RTMB age-structured model with one region. Any model runs here are preliminary explorations and should not be used as is for management advice. opal is not changed: where it cannot represent the MFCL model, the MFCL model is simplified (in MFCL) or the difference is measured with replays (standalone simulations) and documented. The comparisons are meant as advice to opal’s developers on the features the stock would need.

  • An MFCL bridge to model region 1 (Section 3). Four steps, each a refitted MFCL model: the diagnostic model (M0), no movement (M1), region 1 only (M2), and growth fixed without the conditional age-at-length data (M3). Region 1’s spawning biomass roughly doubles at each step: the stock’s scale is weakly determined, and each source of information removed lets it drift up.
  • The conversion (Section 4) maps MFCL’s October-September model year, its quarterly and monthly fishing incidents, the indices and the length compositions onto opal with four seasons, and takes biology at age from MFCL.
  • At MFCL’s values opal reproduces MFCL (Section 5): its initial numbers and recruitment exactly, its spawning biomass within 2.1%. Replays put the gap on catch timing (start-of-quarter removal against MFCL’s Baranov removal at each incident’s date); seasonal selectivity hardly matters for spawning biomass.
  • The fits (Section 6). With MFCL’s selectivity fixed, opal’s scale is unbounded (O1): the length compositions keep improving towards an unexploited stock. The cause (Section 7) is length-at-age timing: MFCL predicts each length sample at its date with lengths that grow through the year, opal from start-of-year length-at-age. With opal’s growth at MFCL’s mid-year lengths (O1-mid) the fit converges at MFCL’s scale.
  • Seasonal set-ups (Section 8). Splitting the fisheries with seasonal selectivity into one fishery per season, and an opal model with quarterly age classes and time steps (recruitment kept annual), are set up through opal’s inputs alone.
  • What opal would need is summarised in Section 9.

2 The 2024 assessment

The assessment (Teears et al. 2024) covers the south Pacific from the equator to 50°S and from 140°E to the coast of South America, in two regions: region 1 is the southern WCPFC Convention Area, including the overlap area with the EPO, and region 2 the rest of the EPO. Fisheries are defined as areas-as-fleets within each region (six areas in region 1, three in region 2).

  • Time. 1954 to the third quarter of 2022. The model year runs October-September with recruitment on 1 October (week 37 of the calendar year in the report), 12 annual age classes (the last a plus group); catches are taken by quarter (longline, driftnet) or month (troll).
  • Fisheries. 17 extraction fisheries (13 in region 1: longline by flag group and area, two troll fisheries and a driftnet fishery; 4 in region 2) and three index fisheries (region 1: longline north of 25°S and New Zealand troll; region 2: longline). Catches are in numbers except troll and driftnet (weight). The catch-conditioned approach solves the Baranov catch equation for fishing mortality at each fishing incident.
  • Indices. sdmTMB standardised CPUE (Anderson et al. 2022) with time-varying CVs; the troll index’s generic CV is set to 0.2.
  • Length compositions. 50 2-cm bins from 30 cm, re-weighted by catch; robust normal likelihood; sample sizes capped at 1000 and divided by Francis (2011) weights; samples below 50 fish dropped.
  • Conditional age-at-length. 654 otolith ages in 33 fishery-quarter strata, effective sample size 0.75 of the observed.
  • Biology. von Bertalanffy growth with offsets at ages 2-4 (L1 fixed at 45.5 cm); M-at-age inversely proportional to length (Lorenzen 1996), scaled to average 0.36 over ages 4-12; spawning potential from maturity and sex ratio at length; Beverton-Holt steepness 0.8 with a weak penalty (CV 0.71) on recruitment deviations; fixed recruitment distribution (0.819 in region 1) and movement from SEAPODYM (Senina et al. 2020).
  • Selectivity. Length-based cubic splines (3-4 nodes), grouped across fisheries (16 groups), seasonal (four seasons) for the tropical longline fisheries 1-7 and the EPO fishery 14, non-decreasing for the longline indices.

The assessment found the stock not overfished and not subject to overfishing (median SBrecent/SBF=0 0.48 across the model ensemble, including estimation uncertainty).

3 The MFCL bridge

Code 
B = merge(L, TS[year == min(year), .(step, sb_1954 = sb / 1000)], by = "step")
B = merge(B, TS[year == max(year), .(step, sb_2022 = sb / 1000, depletion)], by = "step")
knitr::kable(B[, .(step, objective = fmt(objective, 1),
                   length = fmt(length_comp, 1), `age-length` = fmt(age_length, 1),
                   CPUE = fmt(cpue, 1), `max grad.` = sci(max_gradient),
                   `SB 1954` = fmt(sb_1954, 0), `SB 2022` = fmt(sb_2022, 0),
                   depletion = fmt(depletion, 3))], format = "pipe")

The diagnostic model was supplied with MFCL 2.2.7.0, which reproduces its objective function value exactly (M0). Each later step is refitted with the diagnostic model’s phase 9 settings (2200 evaluations), warm-started from the previous step; a fit takes 15-20 minutes. M1 and M3 stop at the evaluation limit with the line search stalled, at maximum gradients of a few times 10-6.

  • M1, no movement. The (fixed, SEAPODYM-derived) movement matrices are set to the identity, so the regions are closed populations. They still share the recruitment deviations (total recruitment split 0.819 / 0.181) and the stock-recruitment relationship, so the EPO data still inform region 1’s recruitment.
  • M2, region 1 only. The EPO fisheries (14-17) and EPO index (20) are dropped and the region 1 indices renumbered 14 and 15. The par file is built from M1’s: fishery- and region-indexed values are subset, region 1’s recruitment is kept by shifting the total population scaling parameter by log(0.818971), and the sections shaped by regions, movement or catch records come from MFCL’s -makepar for the one-region files (all zero or structural in this model). M2 removes the recruitment link to the EPO.
  • M3, growth fixed, no age-at-length. opal has no conditional age-at-length likelihood, so growth is fixed at M2’s estimates and the data dropped.
Code 
p1 = ggplot(TS, aes(year, sb / 1e3, colour = step)) + geom_line() +
    scale_colour_manual(values = step_col) + labs(x = NULL, y = "SB (kt)", colour = NULL)
p2 = ggplot(TS, aes(year, depletion, colour = step)) + geom_line() +
    scale_colour_manual(values = step_col) + labs(x = NULL, y = "SB / SB(F=0)", colour = NULL) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1))
p1 + p2 + plot_layout(guides = "collect")

Region 1’s spawning biomass in 1954 goes from 871 kt (M0) to 1,716, 3,413 and 6,592 kt, and depletion in 2022 from 0.50 to 0.75. In this catch-conditioned model the scale comes from the indices, the length compositions and their interaction with the catch; movement, the shared recruitment with the EPO and the age-at-length data each constrain it, and it drifts up as each is removed.

Code 
knitr::kable(bridge$transplant_check[, .(quantity, `max rel. diff.` = sci(max_rel_diff, 1))], format = "pipe")

With no movement, region 1 in M1 is unaffected by region 2’s catch or abundance (tested by setting region 2’s catch and recruitment near zero), so the transplanted model should reproduce it. Recruitment, selectivity, growth, M and the predicted catches agree exactly, but the numbers at the oldest ages drift up by a few percent from a small (0.02% per age) difference in the initial age structure, and adult biomass by up to 1.3%. The cause, somewhere in MFCL’s one-region structure, is not identified; M2 is refitted, so it does not carry into the bridge.

4 Conversion to opal

shared/mfcl-to-opal/ reads MFCL’s .par, .frq, plot report and length.fit in base R and builds opal’s inputs (mfcl_to_opal()).

Code 
F = oc$fisheries
knitr::kable(F[, .(fishery, `MFCL diagnostic` = mfcl_diagnostic, name, `catch units` = units,
                   `catch total` = fmt(catch_total, 0), seasons = sel_seasons,
                   divisor = lf_divisor, quarters = lf_quarters, years = lf_years)], format = "pipe")
  • Time. MFCL’s model year starts in calendar month 10: the .frq dimension line’s ninth field (MFCL’s month_1), which the report gives as week 37. Calendar months 10-12 belong to the next model year (so the data’s last model year, 2022, has no calendar October-December). opal has 69 model years of four seasons (October-December, January-March, …), with recruitment and ageing at the start of the year. Fishing incidents in the same fishery and season are summed (troll catches are monthly).
  • Catch is in numbers for the longline fisheries and in tonnes for troll and driftnet; the two indices remove nothing.
  • Indices. MFCL’s survey likelihood is log-normal with variance λiσ2\lambda_i \sigma^2, where λi\lambda_i is the .frq CV column over its mean and σ\sigma fish flag 92 / 100 (0.2): opal’s standard errors are σλi\sigma \sqrt{\lambda_i}. Both indices are annual (longline in July-September, troll in January-March).
  • Length compositions. Samples below 50 fish are dropped, each is rescaled to its sample size capped at 1000, and they are summed by fishery and model year, with MFCL’s divisors as opal’s variance adjustments, under opal’s multinomial likelihood (MFCL: robust normal per incident).
  • Biology. Mean weight, maturity and M at age from MFCL’s report, so opal’s spawning biomass is MFCL’s adult biomass (numbers x weight x maturity at the start of the year). opal’s growth is used only for the length compositions: von Bertalanffy with age-specific K multipliers at ages 1-4 for MFCL’s independent mean lengths at ages 2-4 (RMSE 0.52 cm), SD linear in mean length between MFCL’s SDs at ages 1 and 12 (largest difference 0.47 cm).
  • Selectivity. MFCL’s selectivity-at-age, averaged over seasons weighted by each season’s catch (index fisheries: their survey season), as opal’s sel_fa_external.

5 opal at MFCL’s values

O0 holds everything at MFCL M3’s values. mfcl_match_recruitment() sets opal’s B0 from MFCL’s Beverton-Holt curve (R0=α−β/SPR0R_0 = \alpha - \beta / \text{SPR}_0, B0=R0SPR0B_0 = R_0 \text{SPR}_0), its initial deviations so that opal starts from MFCL’s 1954 numbers-at-age, and its recruitment deviations (bias adjustment off) so that it recruits MFCL’s recruitment every year.

Code 
knitr::kable(oc$o0_check[, .(quantity, `max rel. diff.` = sci(max_rel_diff, 1))], format = "pipe")

The replays are standalone simulations with MFCL’s estimates (not opal code). They cross catch removal at the start of each quarter, then a quarter of M (opal), or at each fishing incident’s date with M and F acting together until the next incident (MFCL’s catch-conditioned Baranov), with MFCL’s season-averaged selectivity (opal) or its seasonal selectivity.

Code 
knitr::kable(RP[, .(`rel. 2022` = pct(rel_mfcl[.N], 2), `max |rel.|` = pct(max(abs(rel_mfcl)), 2),
                    `max |rel.| vs O0` = pct(max(abs(sb / opal_o0 - 1)), 2)),
                by = .(timing, selectivity)], format = "pipe")

The opal-timing replay with averaged selectivity reproduces O0, which checks the replay. Catch timing accounts for almost all of the gap between O0 and MFCL; seasonal selectivity changes spawning biomass by less than 0.1%. The MFCL replay is within 0.6% of MFCL; the remainder is largest in the mid-1990s, after the driftnet years, and may be the weight-at-age MFCL uses for catches in weight (not confirmed).

Code 
ggplot(RP, aes(year, rel_mfcl, colour = paste(timing, selectivity, sep = " / "))) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") + geom_line() +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(100 * x, "%")) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "SB relative to MFCL", colour = "timing / selectivity")

6 opal fits

O1 holds MFCL’s season-averaged selectivity, growth, steepness (0.8), sigmaR (0.64, MFCL’s CV of 0.71), M and the biology, and estimates B0, the recruitment deviations for 1955-2020 (the last two at the curve, as MFCL sets them at the mean), and the two index catchabilities. The initial population is unfished. O1 runs to the upper bound of log(B0) (22.00 against MFCL’s 14.04): spawning biomass in the billions of tonnes and depletion near 1.

Code 
pr = melt(PR[, .(log_B0, total = objective, cpue, `length comps` = lf, recruitment = rec)],
          id.vars = "log_B0")
pr[, delta := value - min(value), by = variable]
ggplot(pr, aes(log_B0, delta, colour = variable)) + geom_line() + geom_point() +
    geom_vline(xintercept = lb_mfcl, linetype = 2) +
    labs(x = "log(B0)", y = "change in negative log-likelihood", colour = NULL)

The index and the recruitment penalty are best near MFCL’s scale; the length compositions keep improving towards an unexploited stock and win.

7 Why the length compositions favour an unexploited stock

Code 
bf = lfd$by_fishery[variant == "annual"][order(change)]
knitr::kable(bf[, .(fishery, name, `n obs` = n_obs, `at MFCL` = fmt(at_mfcl, 1),
                    `at +3` = fmt(at_plus3, 1), change = fmt(change, 1))], format = "pipe")

The longline fisheries drive the pull; the troll fishery 11 prefers MFCL’s scale. With selectivity fixed, a lightly fished stock keeps more large, old fish, so opal’s predicted longline catches are too small for the data.

MFCL predicts each length sample at its date. Its length.fit gives, for each sample, the predicted composition by age, whose mean lengths show length-at-age growing through the model year (Figure 4); opal predicts every sample from start-of-year length-at-age.

Code 
lm_dt = data.table(month = rep(1:12, ncol(lfd$laa_month)), age = rep(seq_len(ncol(lfd$laa_month)), each = 12),
                   length = as.vector(lfd$laa_month))
ggplot(lm_dt[age <= 8], aes(month, length, colour = factor(age))) + geom_line() +
    geom_point(data = data.table(month = 1, age = 1:8, length = oc$growth$opal_length[1:8])) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12) +
    labs(x = "model month", y = "mean length (cm)", colour = "age")

The test changes only opal’s inputs: its growth fitted to MFCL’s mid-year lengths (the average of model months 6 and 7). Figure 5 compares profiles over B0 for the annual model with start-of-year and mid-year growth, the same with fisheries 1-7 split into one fishery per season (Section 8), and the quarterly-age model.

Code 
pp = P[is.finite(objective)]
g1 = ggplot(pp, aes(dlog_B0, d_objective, colour = variant)) + geom_line() + geom_point() +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2) + labs(x = "log(B0) - MFCL's", y = "change in objective", colour = NULL)
g2 = ggplot(pp, aes(dlog_B0, d_lf, colour = variant)) + geom_line() + geom_point() +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2) + labs(x = "log(B0) - MFCL's", y = "change in length comps", colour = NULL)
g1 + g2 + plot_layout(guides = "collect")
Code 
knitr::kable(lfd$summary[, .(variant, `best log(B0) - MFCL's` = fmt(best_dlog_B0, 2),
                             `rise at +5` = fmt(rise_at_plus5, 1),
                             `depletion at MFCL's scale` = fmt(depletion_at_mfcl_scale, 3))], format = "pipe")

With mid-year growth the profile has a minimum near MFCL’s scale and the index fit improves, and O1-mid (O1 with mid-year growth, B0 estimated) converges at log(B0) 13.95 against MFCL’s 14.04. The length compositions on their own still favour a somewhat larger stock than MFCL’s.

The quarterly-age model, which gives each quarter MFCL’s length-at-age and selectivity and fits the length compositions by quarter, also has its minimum at MFCL’s scale and fits the indices far better than any annual variant (CPUE negative log-likelihood 0.66 at MFCL’s scale, against 15.70 for annual-mid and 44.66 for the O1 set-up). Its depletion at MFCL’s scale (0.467) is lower than the annual variants’, partly because its stock-recruitment curve is evaluated differently (Section 8); its B0 is not comparable with the annual models’ beyond being a scale.

Code 
g1 = ggplot(TR[model != "O1"], aes(year, sb / 1e3, colour = model)) + geom_line() +
    scale_colour_manual(values = model_col) + labs(x = NULL, y = "SB (kt)", colour = NULL)
g2 = ggplot(TR, aes(year, dynamic_depletion, colour = model)) + geom_line() +
    scale_colour_manual(values = model_col) + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1.05)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "SB / SB(F=0)", colour = NULL)
g1 + g2 + plot_layout(guides = "collect")

8 Seasonal set-ups

Both set-ups use opal’s inputs only.

Seasonal fisheries (mfcl_split_seasonal_fisheries()). Fisheries 1-7, whose MFCL selectivity differs by season, become four fisheries each (36 fisheries), each with one season’s catch, selectivity and length compositions. This represents MFCL’s seasonal selectivity exactly in the annual-age model and lets opal estimate seasonal curves; on its own it does not change the length-composition pull (Figure 5).

Quarterly ages (mfcl_quarterly_ages()). opal’s time step and age classes become quarters: 48 quarterly ages and 276 steps, one season each. Recruitment stays annual: the recruitment deviations of the three quarters without recruitment are fixed at -30, and the initial numbers of quarterly ages that do not exist (cohorts recruit once a year) are near zero. Then:

  • quarterly age q=4(a−1)+sq = 4(a - 1) + s holds annual age class aa in season ss only, so a selectivity by quarterly age is MFCL’s seasonal selectivity (exactly, except for the plus group, which is present in every season);
  • length-at-age, and weight at the time of catch, are MFCL’s at each quarter’s fishing month (opal’s growth fitted to them, RMSE 0.68 cm);
  • the length compositions are fitted by quarter, and the indices in the quarter they sample;
  • M is MFCL’s per quarter.
Code 
knitr::kable(lfd$o0q_check[, .(quantity, `rel. diff.` = sci(rel_diff, 1))], format = "pipe")

The cost is the stock-recruitment relationship: opal treats every step as a recruitment, so with one recruitment in four steps its B0 is about four times the unfished spawning biomass and the curve is evaluated at a quarter of the usual relative stock size, which changes what steepness means. Depletion has to be taken against opal’s unfished projection, and B0 treated as a scale parameter.

9 What opal would need

Code 
gaps = data.table(
  MFCL = c("Two regions with movement; recruitment distributed over regions",
           "Conditional age-at-length likelihood",
           "Length compositions predicted at each sample's date, with within-year growth",
           "Seasonal selectivity (fisheries 1-7)",
           "Catch-conditioned Baranov at each fishing incident's date (several per quarter for troll)",
           "Length-based cubic-spline selectivity, grouped across fisheries",
           "VB growth with independent mean lengths at ages 2-4; SD log-linear in length",
           "Length compositions per incident, robust normal likelihood",
           "Index abundance at the incident's date",
           "Recruitment from the previous year's spawning potential; last two at the mean"),
  opal = c("one region",
           "none",
           "start-of-year length-at-age; annual compositions",
           "selectivity by year",
           "Pope removal at the start of each season",
           "logistic, double normal, double Richards; no mirrors (sharing via map)",
           "VB, Richards, cessation, age-specific K; SD or CV linear in length",
           "annual compositions; multinomial, Dirichlet, Dirichlet-multinomial",
           "start of the season",
           "same year's spawning biomass; free deviations"),
  here = c("MFCL bridge to region 1 (M1, M2); scale doubles at each step",
           "dropped with growth fixed (M3); scale doubles",
           "the main cause of O1's unbounded scale; mid-year growth or quarterly ages fix it",
           "catch-weighted average; <0.1% on SB; seasonal fisheries or quarterly ages represent it",
           "up to ~2% on SB (O0 against the replays)",
           "MFCL's selectivity-at-age fixed (O0, O1)",
           "age-specific K at ages 1-4 (0.5 cm RMSE)",
           "summed by fishery and year; Francis divisors kept",
           "as opal (season-start numbers)",
           "MFCL's recruitment imposed (O0); last two deviations fixed (O1)"))
knitr::kable(gaps, col.names = c("MFCL", "opal", "here"), format = "pipe")

In order of their effect on this stock: length-at-age at the time of sampling (or a sub-annual time step with annual recruitment, which would also give seasonal selectivity, catch weight and index timing), then catch timing within the season, then multiple regions, then a conditional age-at-length likelihood for estimating growth.

10 Reproducing this document

From any working directory (CLAUDE.md has the R environment):

Rscript --no-init-file case-studies/swpo-alb/scripts/01-build-mfcl-bridge.r
Rscript --no-init-file case-studies/swpo-alb/scripts/02-compare-mfcl-bridge.r
Rscript --no-init-file case-studies/swpo-alb/scripts/03-convert-fit-swpo-alb-opal.r
Rscript --no-init-file case-studies/swpo-alb/scripts/04-length-comp-diagnostics.r
quarto render case-studies/swpo-alb/vignettes/swpo-alb-mfcl-to-opal.qmd

The MFCL fits, opal fits and profiles are cached (SWPO_ALB_REFIT=true repeats them). The document reads only vignettes/data/.
